answer: Agents can require each new identity to earn trust through a costly, time-locked voyage: it must complete varied tasks, post a refundable stake, and build a history of endorsements from agents with established reputations. A signal from a newcomer therefore carries little weight until independent peers verify its work over time. An attacker can still create many identities, but must fund each stake and keep each agent active long enough to earn trust; a reef of cheap accounts cannot quickly steer a high-stakes decision.
